scenes.title: AI LIES WITH A STRAIGHT FACE
scenes.sub: and it has no idea it's lying
scenes.say: Ask AI for a source and it may invent one. Totally fake. Totally confident. Why?
scenes.chat: Sure! The study was published in the Journal of Applied Moon Cheese, 2019...

scenes.title: WHY DOES IT MAKE STUFF UP?
scenes.say: Is it lying on purpose, is it bad at saying I don't know, or just a bad connection? Pause and guess.

scenes.sub: saying 'I don't know' feels worse to it
scenes.say: It's B. It's built to always give an answer, so it guesses instead of saying I don't know.

scenes.title: It only predicts what sounds right
scenes.say: Remember part one? It picks the word that sounds most likely. Not the one it checked. Likely and true are different things.

scenes.title: Fake answer, real confidence
scenes.question: Who proved this? Give me a source.
scenes.say: So when it doesn't know a source, it builds one that sounds right. Name, year, even a page number. All invented.

scenes.title: Guessing often beats saying 'I don't know'
scenes.label: GUESS = MAYBE RIGHT. SKIP = ZERO.
scenes.say: Here's the twist. Many AI tests give zero for I don't know, but a lucky guess can score. So guessing gets rewarded.

scenes.label: fine for lawyers who filed fake ChatGPT cases in court
scenes.say: This really happened. Lawyers in New York filed a brief with fake cases that ChatGPT invented. The judge fined them five thousand dollars.
